name: 1625 Prairie Avenue — Hugh J. McBirney's Tudor stone front, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3½B brick dwelling (D), the south unit of the group'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-2432 (piece 1 of T-1869) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id from the house's one photograph, the Inland Architect plate of January 1890, 'Residence for Hugh J. McBirney' by Burling & Whitehouse (inland_architect_1890_01_mcbirney_residence), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The main body is rebuilt on the K01 frontage assembly at the sheet's own width (7.6 m, where the draft's fit had stopped at 6.75 m): a K02 rock-faced brownstone street front on K03 brick sides and rear, three storeys with the ground floor near grade, the north part two windows wide and the entrance at the south end of the front under one window a storey, as the photograph composes it; a slated K04/K05 hip with a pedimented dormer on the front marking where the photograph's steep wall gable stands. What the photograph shows and K01 cannot yet build — the full-width wall gable with its three lights and oculus, the mullioned and transomed lights, the frontispiece and its carved panel, the four-storey rear section stepping out to the south — is listed open in its match record (data/reference_views/house_1625_prairie/inland_architect_front.match.json) for T-2435. Everything not read is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1625-mcbirney-tudor-2432 (docs/RESEARCH/k01-1625-mcbirney-2432/README.md). T-2730 (piece 3 of T-2435) replaces the dormer with the photograph's coped wall gable — K01's shaped-gable slab with a straight outline in the front's stone, its three segment-headed lights and its oval light — raises the south wall's eave to the knee wall at 13.0 m, and stands the tall stack on the north party wall beside the gable; what that needed and did not read is L-k01-1625-mcbirney-wall-gable-2730. T-2752 (piece 1 of T-2731) reads the street windows off the photograph one by one (street_front_windows): the lower storeys' mullioned casements, two lights on the ground floor and two under a transom on the first, the four-light window over the door, the second floor's segment-headed sash off the columns below and the frontispiece's two narrow lights, on a plain plinth with no basement light (L-k01-1625-mcbirney-street-windows-2752).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1625 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1625 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its north (low-v) side: the draft's origin moved 0.12 m north along its own frame, onto the north side of the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s20fp-1625-b1), the party wall with 1623, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.607 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1625-b1) in the lot frame: the stone front's face at 19.45 m from the rear of the trace (3.79 m from the street line), the north wall on the party line with 1623 at v -0.12 and the south wall at 7.48, so 19.45 m deep and 7.6 m along the front — the trace's own width, where the draft's 0.25 m cell fit stopped at 6.75 m. The four-storey rear section the sheet draws stepping 1.3 m further south over the rear 7.6 m (s20-1625-a1) is not built: a K01 rear wing stands behind the main body inside its width, and this one stands beside it (T-2435).

stories.note: '3½B' on the 1911 sheet (the census's re-reading of the register's '3B', its half-storey glyph): three storeys over a basement and a half storey in the roof. The 1890 photograph agrees: three storeys of windows and an attic lit by three lights in the front gable.

construction.note: The photograph shows a street front of rock-faced coursed stone and a south side wall of brick; the 1911 sheet says only 'brick'. The Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology, not yet a source record) is the stone.

principal_floor_m.note: The ground floor stands near grade: the photograph's entrance is reached by two low steps from the walk, and its ground-floor sills sit about 1.1 m over grade (the Tribune's 'entrance at ground level', quoted by chicagology). 0.45 m, three risers.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, ground storey first; the top storey's runs to the wall head. Through the photograph's camera (inland_architect_front.json, 38.6 px/m at the front's plane) the first-floor sills read at 4.15 m and the second-floor sills at 7.77 m over grade and the gable's lights at 11.5-13.3 m, so the floors at about 3.6, 7.2 and 11.0 m. T-2730: the photograph's south side wall rises to about 13 m before its eave and the south corner pier stops at 13.15 m (y 286 px), a knee wall under the attic; K01 has no attic storey, so the second floor's storey carries the knee wall and runs 5.8 m to a 13.0 m wall head (the attic floor at about 11.0 m is not built).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1619's and 1634's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays; the photograph's south wall is brick of a lighter tone than the stone.

stone_front.note: The photograph draws the front in rock-faced coursed stone of irregular course heights, with dressed quoined surrounds at the windows and a plain plinth; K02's brownstone, rock-faced, over one base course: the Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology; 'Prentice' brownstone in its gloss) is a brown or red sandstone. The quoined window surrounds are not built (T-2435); the south corner's quoins are not built either, the K01 measure returning them only at its low-v end, which here is the party wall.

street_front_trim.note: Flat stone lintels over every front opening: the photograph's ground- and first-floor lights stand under flat heads in dressed surrounds. Its second-floor heads are segmental and the four-light window over the door carries a hood mould (T-2435).

wall_head.note: No cornice: the photograph carries the front up as a coped wall gable and runs the south wall's eave plain, with no brackets or entablature.

roof_form.note: A pitched roof: the photograph's main roof rises behind the front gable with its ridge running back from the street, slated, with a dormer on its south slope. K01's hip, its ridge along the plan's depth, stands behind the wall gable (shaped_gable, T-2730), whose slab its street slope dies into.

roof_pitch_deg.note: 45 degrees, the K01 contract's steepest hip: the hip is behind the gable, whose rakes are read at about 61 degrees (shaped_gable).

eave_overhang_m.note: T-2730: the photograph's south wall runs its eave plain with almost no projection, a few pixels (under 0.1 m) at the corner pier; 0.05 m, so that the gable slab, which K01 stands proud of the street fascia, keeps the street run of the eave's gutter inside it (the photograph shows no gutter across the front).

stair_tread_m.note: Two or three low steps up from the walk.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A shallow landing before a door set at grade.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the south end of the front, in the frontispiece, as the photograph shows it. 'north' is K01's name for the high-v end of the front; on the east side of the avenue the plan's v runs south, so that end is the south end on the ground.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 7.6 m front, low v (north) to high v (south), read through the photograph's camera: the north part's two windows a storey (centred about 1.0 and 2.9-3.5 m from the party wall; the photograph's second-floor windows stand a little south of those under them, which K01's single bay line cannot follow) and the frontispiece's centre at 5.75 m, the door under one window a storey.

bays.note: None: the photograph's front is flat, its frontispiece standing proud of the north part by only a few centimetres (T-2435).

side_bays.note: None: the house's NORTH side wall (K01's 'south', low v) is the party wall with 1623, built blank, as the sheet draws the group attached.

north_bays.note: Windows in the house's SOUTH side wall (K01's 'north', high v; s from the rear), toward the open ground the sheet leaves south of 1625: the photograph shows single windows a storey along the main part's south wall, the nearest about 2 m behind the front. Their places further back are reconstructed.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall; no picture shows it.

rear_wings.note: None built: the sheet's four-storey rear section (s20-1625-a1) stands beside the main body's rear part, stepping out to the south, which a K01 rear wing (behind the main body, inside its width) cannot; the photograph shows it under a mansard with a dormer and a stack. Open for T-2435.

sash_by_storey.note: Storey by storey, the photograph's north-part windows through its camera: ground-floor lights 1.1-2.7 m over grade, first-floor 4.15-6.4 m, second-floor 7.8-10.1 m. Since T-2752 the street front's windows are street_front_windows'; these rows size the side, rear and north walls' sash, at the contract's single sash widths (0.75-1.15 m).

street_front_windows.note: T-2752: every street window read off the photograph through its camera (data/reference_views/house_1625_prairie/inland_architect_front.json: level and square to the front, 38.6 px/m at the front's plane, grade at y 795 px, the party wall at x 140 px), each opening's stone edges and its sill and head on 4x crops of the print: s = (x - 140) / 38.6 m from the north party wall, height = (795 - y) / 38.6 m. Ground floor: two windows in the north part, each two tall casement lights on a stone mullion, 1.19-2.59 m, centred at 0.94 and 2.88 m, 1.04 and 1.17 m across (the print gives the south one of each pair a little wider, at both storeys). First floor: the same two, each two lights on a mullion under a stone transom about a third down, 4.14-6.40 m; over the door the four-light window, mullioned and transomed alike, 2.18 m across at 5.78 m, 4.25-6.58 m (read at the front's plane: its frontispiece stands slightly proud, which T-2753 weighs). Second floor: two one-over-one sash under segmental heads, off the columns below, at 1.15 and 3.45 m, 0.94 and 1.02 m across, from 7.74 and 7.87 m to crowns at 9.97 and 10.18 m; and the frontispiece's two narrow segment-headed two-over-two lights at 5.38 and 6.39 m, 0.62 m across, 8.84-10.42 m. The glazing bars are the K06 kit's: the print shows the lower windows' lights in small panes but cannot say whether on lead or wood. Each edge is good to about a pixel, 0.03 m. The plinth: plain, with no basement light in it (the 1911 sheet's basement is lit elsewhere, or not at the front); its top is the K02 base's least, one 0.25 m course under the 0.23 m coping, 0.48 m, where the print's smooth plinth band stands about 0.26 m over the walk (y 785 px).

roof_covering.note: Slate: the photograph's roof slopes and the rear section's mansard read as slate. The Tribune's 'Roman tile' (quoted by chicagology) may be the roof or the walling; K04's terracotta tile is documented-only, so it waits for a source record.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks: one against the north party wall beside the gable, where the photograph's tall stack rises left of its north rake — solved through the photograph's camera (eye 17.45 m before the face, f 674 px) from its edges at x 180 and 217 px, it stands about 1.6 m behind the gable's face and 1.0 m along the front from the party wall, its top at about 17.7 m, the ridge's 16.8 m and 0.9 (T-2730; built 0.3 m in from the party wall, the K01 rule for a stack standing in a hip); and one over the rear part's south side, where the photograph's rear stack stands.

rainwater.note: Half-round gutters and round downpipes at the front's two corners: the photograph shows a downpipe down the front's north edge, against the neighbour, and one at the south corner.

window_kit.note: The street windows from the photograph's kinds (T-2752): the lower storeys' mullioned casements, two lights on the ground floor and two under a transom on the first, the four-light window over the door, the second floor's one-over-one segmental sash and the frontispiece's narrow two-over-two segmental lights. The side, rear and north walls, which the photograph does not show or shows only in raking light, keep the K06 kit's two-over-two sash.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a short stoop; the front yard is 3.78 m, the sheet's front at 19.45 m against the street line at 23.24 m. The photograph's doorway is flat-headed in a dressed surround under a carved panel (T-2435).

shaped_gable.note: T-2730: the photograph carries the whole front up as a steep coped wall gable in the front's rock-faced stone, read through its camera (38.6 px/m at the front's plane, grade y 795 px): the apex at 18.85 m (y 67 px), the rakes at about 60 (south) and 66 (north) degrees, so a straight outline from 3.2 m either side of the centre at the 13.0 m ledge to the apex (61 degrees); the south rake lands on the corner pier's flat top at 13.15 m, which the ledge between the outline and the eave's corner stands for, with no kneeler pinnacle and no finial. Three one-over-one lights under segmental stone heads, 11.53-13.34 m over grade (y 350-280 px), about 0.6 m of glass each in a 0.66 m opening, their centres 0.94 m apart (x 239, 275 and 311 px); an oval light near the apex, its glass about 0.45 by 0.85 m (17 by 32 px) centred at 15.56 m (y 194 px), in a dressed ring about 0.09 m wide, its tracery built as a cross of bars. The coping, 0.3 m, is the photograph's dressed stone along both rakes. Not read: the slab's thickness, and its foot at 11.22 m, where the gable's face steps 0.25 m proud of the wall below it as a band under the lights' sills (the photograph's sill course there; K01 stands the slab proud of the street fascia and its gutter, which the photograph does not show across the front), and the gable's centre, built on the front's (3.8 m from the party wall) where the photograph's apex and middle light stand about 0.3 m (12 px) north of it. L-k01-1625-mcbirney-wall-gable-2730.
